outputThat: **Structural boundary:** Part I contains exclusively mandatory SHALL imperatives. Part II contains independently organized SHOULD procedures, concrete examples and descriptive contract facts. Procedures do not grant authority or override imperatives.

19:- **SP-03:** Creation SHALL publish a JSON template comment containing a header object and nonempty entries array of caption/work objects; it SHALL return comment ID, Issue number, URL and revision.
25:- **SP-09:** Each create/edit or subject transition SHALL have a versioned caption; work text SHALL reside in the entry's work member.
33:- **PC-01:** A program instance SHALL own its designated **control-comment ID** exclusively while active. This SHALL be distinct from permanent **scratchpad data-comment IDs**.
34:- **PC-02:** Allocation SHALL bind a control-comment ID to a unique instance ID and monotonically increasing generation in durable program-session state.
35:- **PC-03:** On completion or termination, the program SHALL release the control-comment binding and mark the comment available for another instance.
36:- **PC-04:** A new instance SHALL be able to acquire a released comment ID with a new instance ID and incremented generation.
37:- **PC-05:** Every session-scoped operation SHALL verify control-comment ID, instance ID and generation; stale instance commands SHALL be rejected.
38:- **PC-06:** Release SHALL be idempotent for the same already-ended instance and SHALL NOT affect a newer owner.

39:- **PC-07:** The durable lease state SHALL use an optimistic compare-and-swap update to prevent simultaneous allocation of a single control comment. Lease state SHALL be authoritative if UI rendering becomes stale.
40:- **PC-08:** Completing or terminating a program SHALL NOT delete, truncate, recycle or rewrite its persistent scratchpad data comments.

41:- **PC-09:** A program instance SHALL remain active across separate commands and workflow runs until completed, terminated or explicitly recovered. Finishing one command SHALL NOT automatically end the instance.
42:- **PC-10:** Start, status and release responses SHALL identify the control-comment ID, instance ID, generation and current status.
45:The lifecycle is: available → active → completed/terminated → available → active (new instance, new generation). The numeric control-comment ID is reusable; its ownership is not.

47:The program SHALL distinguish **control** comments used for menus and transient interaction from **data** comments carrying permanent scratchpad entries. The control-comment registry SHALL be persisted at workspaces/programs/sessions/state.json. The concrete release API SHALL use programInput operations complete and terminate with the current control_comment_id, instance_id, and generation. An explicit recover operation SHALL require the current generation and a reason.

49:**Example:** Instance A acquires control comment 123 (generation 4), then completes. Instance B subsequently acquires comment 123 (generation 5). A subsequent request carrying A's instance ID or generation 4 SHALL be rejected as STALE_INSTANCE. A's scratchpad data-comment ID remains unchanged.

62:**Scratchpad operations:** \`new\`, \`edit\`, \`new_entry\`, \`edit_entry\`, \`submit_json\`. An empty programInput returns the application operation menu. \`edit\` with a comment ID returns its entry selection menu. New entry is selection ID zero; existing active entries occupy subsequent IDs. Mutating operations accept \`expected_revision\` to detect stale snapshots.
